title: Hidden Stories of AI, episode 3: the artists who painted with machines
summary: Harold Cohen's AARON, the AI portrait that sold for $432,500 at Christie's, and Refik Anadol's machine dreams at MoMA.
ticker: HIDDEN STORIES OF AI · EPISODE 3 · ART · COHEN · OBVIOUS · ANADOL

say: Can a machine make art? Artists have been testing that question for more than fifty years.
Starting in the early 1970s, the British painter Harold Cohen built AARON, a program that made its own drawings.
He kept teaching it for decades, until it could draw figures and plants, and add colour.
In 2018, a Paris collective called Obvious sold an AI-made portrait at Christie's in New York.
Expected to fetch up to 10,000 dollars, it sold for 432,500.
The AI had learned from 15,000 old portraits, and much of the code came from a 19-year-old artist, Robbie Barrat.
In 2022, the Turkish-American artist Refik Anadol showed Unsupervised at the Museum of Modern Art in New York.
An AI trained on the museum's own collection dreamed new images on a giant wall, changing with the light, movement and weather around it.
A painter's program, a sold portrait, a dreaming museum. The question is still open.
